name: Dexketoprofen
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Dexketoprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) excreted mainly in urine as glucuronide. NSAIDs can cause fluid retention, hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury. The Irish label starts at 50 mg/day in mild kidney impairment (creatinine clearance [CrCl] 60–89 mL/min) and contraindicates it at CrCl 59 mL/min or below. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Irish summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min); thresholds 89 and 59.

bands.recommendation: CrCl ≥90: 25 mg every 8 hours, maximum 75 mg/day, shortest course. CrCl 60–89: start at 50 mg/day total (SmPC). Injection: 50 mg every 8 to 12 hours, maximum 150 mg/day, no more than 2 days; CrCl 60–89: 50 mg/day total (injection SmPC).
Contraindicated: moderate to severe kidney dysfunction (CrCl ≤59 mL/min) (oral and injection SmPCs).

pd.text: Contraindicated (CrCl ≤59; SmPC). NSAIDs also hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Contraindicated (CrCl ≤59; SmPC); NSAIDs worsen acute kidney injury.

monitoring: Kidney function, potassium and fluid status, especially with diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs or volume depletion; keep the patient hydrated. Gastrointestinal bleeding. Shortest course (SmPC 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Not to be used in children and adolescents (SmPC).

renal.recommendation: Not established in children; kidney dosing not applicable.
